newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil standoff deepens, diesel barges firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil standoff deepens, diesel barges firm.

text.p: NWE gas oil trade was virtually static for the third straight day on Friday as traders sat back in a war of nerves with the major long on the November IPE futures expiry.
"It's a massive standoff," one trader said. "People will not trade second half November because they are waiting to see what the outcome of this play will be."

Dec IPE futures finished up $1.50 at $220.75 but heating oil premiums were unchanged. Values were notional as most traders held back in an attempt to assess whether the long wanted takers in NWE for the material from the record 861,500 tonne delivery.
Some traders said they expected the long to agree to washouts or alternative delivery procedures but others said the long planned to place the product in its own system and in Asia.

"He (the long) is not going to dump this product. He has no interest in doing washouts. He is forcing the issue and wants to take all of the barrels into his own system (in France and Germany)," one trader said.
Barge low sulphur premiums firmed $3 to Dec +$16 on better demand but cargo premiums were stable at Dec IPE +$16/18. Heating oil barges were Dec +$4/6, cargoes at +$9/11.
